# `Ffi.Rust`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Ffi.Rust — the taxonomy-native surface for calling a linked Rust crate.

Mental model: after `ipe rust add <crate>` links a Rust crate into the
project, a top-level Ipê definition can ASSERT a single call into it. The
assertion is point-free — the annotation is the whole contract, the body
names the crate and the item beneath it:

```ipe
import Ipe.Ffi.Rust as Rust

sha256 : Bytes -> Bytes
sha256 =
    Rust.fn "sha2" "Sha256::digest"
```

The build driver inspects the linked crate, generates a typed forwarder plus
a `_bindings.rs` shim, and the resolver rewrites the `Rust.fn` call onto that
forwarder. Your code sees an ordinary annotated Ipê value.

Trust boundary — an asserted call is fail-closed at every step, never an
ambient FFI capability:

  * The two literals are PARSED, not validated: an empty, single-segment, or
    non-identifier path is unrepresentable (it never reaches generated Rust).
    The crate half must be one identifier — `Rust.fn "a::b" "c"` is refused,
    not silently read as `a::b::c`.
  * A binding is admitted ONLY when the target crate is actually installed
    (`ipe rust add`) and the whole body is the single asserted call under a
    top-level annotation. A missing crate or a malformed body fails to
    compile — there is no partial or best-effort binding.
  * The forwarder's type is the annotation's type; the driver's inspection
    must agree with it, or the emitted crate does not build (the ipe-accepts
    ⇒ cargo-builds seal). You cannot give a native item the wrong Ipê type.

This module documents that surface for discoverability (`ipe doc`). It is a
compiler-internal qualifier: importing it does not by itself grant FFI — the
crate-installed and vouched-origin gates above still apply.

Companion surface — `foreign` declarations. A `foreign` top-level declares an
Ipê-held Rust TYPE (a struct, enum, or closure handle) as inert data the CLI
lifts into the binding manifest:

```ipe
foreign Version =
    { crate = "semver", kind = Struct }
```

The compiler treats a `foreign` declaration as inert — it takes no part in
name resolution, type-checking, or lowering — so it is documented in prose
here rather than as a value member of this module.

A closure handle carries an Ipê function into Rust. Its declared return is the
only channel a failure inside the Ipê function can take back to the Rust
caller. With a `Result` return, a runtime limit (recursion depth, an output
ceiling) arrives as an `Err` the caller can recover from. With an `Option` or
a bare scalar return there is no channel for it, so the limit ends the program
with its typed error (exit status 1). A panic inside the Rust code itself
still yields `None` from an `Option` closure. Declare `Result` wherever the
caller must survive a limit, such as one failing request in a server.

## `fn`

```ipe
fn : String -> String -> a
```

`fn "<crate>" "<item>"` — assert a call into a linked Rust function.

`"<crate>"` is the installed crate (one Rust identifier); `"<item>"` is the
item beneath it (`Sha256::digest`, `frobnicate`). Written point-free under a
full annotation, which is the binding's whole type contract:

```ipe
shift : Int -> Int
shift =
    Rust.fn "tm" "shift"
```

The driver generates a typed forwarder for the item and the resolver rewrites
this call onto it. Admitted only when the crate is installed via `ipe rust
add` and the definition's whole body is this call under a top-level
annotation; anything else fails closed.

## `const`

```ipe
const : String -> String -> a
```

`const "<crate>" "<item>"` — read an infallible native constant of a bare
scalar type from a linked Rust crate.

Distinct from `fn`: a constant is a bare value read (no `Result`, no unit
parameter, no arguments), so it is written under a scalar annotation and
applied to nothing:

```ipe
pi : Float
pi =
    Rust.const "std" "f64::consts::PI"
```

The two-literal `"<crate>" "<item>"` path spelling and the crate-installed /
vouched-origin gates are shared with `fn`; only the accepted shape differs —
applying a `const` to a value argument is refused fail-closed.
